title: Dannion Brinkley's holographic life review
summary: Rizwan Virk tells of Dannion Brinkley's holographic life review, about after the Vietnam War at near-death experience, and relays what a named person told them. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: So, Dannion Brinkley called it a holographic panoramic, three-dimensional review of your life. And so, you have to replay every moment. But, what happens is you have to replay it not from your own perspective, but from the perspective of other people in your life. So, he was in the military and actually, you know, killed people during the Vietnam War. He had experienced what it was like to take a bullet from himself.

plain: A computer scientist from MIT, Rizwan Virk, tells on podcast host Jesse Michels' show what a man named Dannion Brinkley says he went through in a near-death experience. Brinkley called it a holographic, three-dimensional replay of his whole life, seen not from his own eyes but from the eyes of the people he affected. Virk says Brinkley, who had been a soldier and killed people in the Vietnam War, felt what it was like to take a bullet from himself, which Virk offers as a hint that reality may work like a recording or simulation.
